$ edit testdata/top0/base.txtar  # a base at Top0

        l3 ran on base

$ go test  # cycle-a
    the lift l3 is used by ./b on the path testdata/top1/ → l2b → l3, and ., which owns it, doesn't run it over testdata/top1/, so no package writes its cells of that corpus's cases, which ./b's cells past it are built through.
        A package that uses a lift reaches it from each corpus by the path the lift's owner does: either . runs l3 over testdata/top1/ by that path, or ./b doesn't reach l3 from testdata/top1/. Making a way true may need other registrations to change, such as a lift that would then close a cycle or give a type a second path. If one holds already, a registry is stale: run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./..., which rewrites the registry of every package with tests.
    what ran, in order:
        l2 ran on base
        l3 ran on base
        l1 ran
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/top0
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/top0/base
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/top0/base/l1
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/top0/base/l2
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/top0/base/l3
FAIL
[exit 1]
